\section{WebCoder --- Administrator
Guide}\label{webcoder--administrator-guide}

\begin{quote}
One-paragraph summary: Administrators run the content engine (curation
queues, approvals, rejudging, imports) and the safety engine
(moderation, reports with SLAs, appeals, integrity scans) plus platform
operations (status, backups, throttles, the optional AI curator). This
guide covers every admin surface and the management commands behind
them.
\end{quote}

\textbf{Who it\textquotesingle s for:} platform ADMINs and VERIFIERs.
Romanian twin:
\href{../guide-ro/GHID-ADMIN.md}{\texttt{docs/guide-ro/GHID-ADMIN.md}}.

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection{1. The admin dashboard}\label{1-the-admin-dashboard}

\texttt{/admin/dashboard} --- counts, plus the operational tabs:
submissions browser (verdict filter, \textbf{Rejudge} button),
stuck-submission monitor (PENDING/COMPILING/RUNNING older than N
minutes), user management (role changes --- the only place roles move),
and metrics snapshot (\texttt{/api/v1/admin/metrics/}: queue depth,
verdict distribution, 24 h judge-duration stats).

\subsection{2. Content curation}\label{2-content-curation}

\subsubsection{Approval queue}\label{approval-queue}

\texttt{/admin/problem-queue} lists \texttt{status=PENDING} problems
with the full context an evaluation needs:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  statement render + lint report + readability score + translation-gaps
  panel;
\item
  \textbf{Tests row} --- every test\textquotesingle s input/expected
  pair, sample flag, points, subtask, per-test bar, catch rate;
\item
  \textbf{testcase strength} (\texttt{/problems/\{id\}/test-strength/})
  --- per-test catch rate over known-wrong solutions, suite strength
  (samples excluded), uncalibrated flag;
\item
  approve/reject with feedback (notifies the author; rejections keep the
  problem editable).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Rejudge \& integrity}\label{rejudge--integrity}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Rejudge} (admin platform-wide; VERIFIERs on their own
  problems): resets to PENDING and re-dispatches through the real judge
  lane; per-test outcomes from the first execution are persisted so
  quick score swaps are possible.
\item
  \textbf{Plagiarism/boilerplate scans} --- advisory badges for human
  review, never auto-punish; diff view side-by-side; multi-account IP
  heuristics feed the same queue.
\item
  \textbf{AI-solution labeling} --- post-contest AI-declaration review +
  solve-pattern anomalies (see the integrity wave\textquotesingle s
  queue).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Imports \& catalog ops}\label{imports--catalog-ops}

Management commands (run in the backend container):

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{python}\NormalTok{ manage.py seed\_problems            }\CommentTok{\# starter pack + curriculum + tags}
\ExtensionTok{python}\NormalTok{ manage.py boost\_hidden\_tests       }\CommentTok{\# regenerate hidden suites from committed specs}
\ExtensionTok{python}\NormalTok{ manage.py catalog\_polish           }\CommentTok{\# translation/hygiene payload (idempotent)}
\ExtensionTok{python}\NormalTok{ manage.py catalog\_cleanup }\PreprocessorTok{[{-}{-}}\SpecialStringTok{apply}\PreprocessorTok{]}  \CommentTok{\# e2e/ad{-}hoc fixture leftovers}
\ExtensionTok{python}\NormalTok{ manage.py export\_catalog           }\CommentTok{\# deterministic fixture snapshot}
\ExtensionTok{python}\NormalTok{ manage.py import\_catalog           }\CommentTok{\# rebuild (or {-}{-}from{-}release \textless{}tag\textgreater{})}
\ExtensionTok{python}\NormalTok{ manage.py calibrate\_difficulty     }\CommentTok{\# difficulty from AC rates (CNT{-}3)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

Import provenance: the CNT-2 \texttt{ImportSource} ledger (source,
contact, terms, evidence URL) must have a row before a corpus import is
legitimate.

\subsection{3. Moderation}\label{3-moderation}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Report queue}: every report button (posts, messages, problems,
  submissions) lands here with SLA tracking; actions: resolve/dismiss
  with note.
\item
  \textbf{Appeals}: moderation decisions are appealable; the audit trail
  records handler, action and note.
\item
  \textbf{Abuse contact + bounty page}: \texttt{/security} documents the
  reporting flow; the bug-bounty page formalizes it.
\item
  \textbf{Content filter} (messaging): RO+EN flag-not-block filter ---
  flagged messages queue for review rather than being silently dropped.
\item
  Hide-at-threshold + trust-weighted voting run automatically (small
  negatives render 0; auto-hide with reveal toggle).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{4. The AI curator (optional, OFF by
default)}\label{4-the-ai-curator-optional-off-by-default}

Screens community translation proposals
(\texttt{/api/v1/translations/proposals/}). Configure via env
(\texttt{AI\_CURATOR\_URL} = any OpenAI-compatible endpoint;
\texttt{AI\_CURATOR\_MODEL}; \texttt{AI\_CURATOR\_TIMEOUT\_S} ≤ 30;
\texttt{AI\_CURATOR\_AUTO\_APPROVE=false} default). Policy:
high-confidence passes queue for human confirmation; low confidence
flags; timeouts/errors mark \texttt{ai\_verdict=error} and fall through
to the human queue --- fail-open, humans confirm every approval unless
auto-approve is explicitly on. Any OpenAI-compatible server works
(OpenAI, Azure, vLLM, Ollama\ldots). See RUNBOOK §ai-curator.

\subsection{5. Platform operations}\label{5-platform-operations}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Status page} (\texttt{/status}): live queue depth, judge
  health; the ops wave added queue transparency, autoscale scripts
  (\texttt{scripts/judge-autoscale.sh}) and the load-test harness
  (\texttt{scripts/load\_smoke.py\ -\/-judge},
  \texttt{e2e/loadtest/replay.mjs}).
\item
  \textbf{Backups run by default} (db-backup sidecar; RUNBOOK §Backups):
  trigger manually, list artifacts, restore + verify via
  \texttt{/api/v1/users/admin/stats/} row counts; quarterly restore
  drill script (\texttt{scripts/restore-drill.sh}).
\item
  \textbf{Throttles} are env-tunable (\texttt{THROTTLE\_*});
  redis-backed.
\item
  \textbf{Blue-green deploy} scripts + the contest capacity gate
  (\texttt{manage.py\ contest\_replay\ -\/-contest\ \textless{}id\textgreater{}\ -\/-users\ 50})
  precede any first rated contest.
\item
  \textbf{Email}: console backend by default; set \texttt{EMAIL\_HOST} +
  SPF/DKIM/DMARC before real sends (RUNBOOK §email).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{6. User administration}\label{6-user-administration}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Roles: BASIC / CREATOR / TEACHER / VERIFIER / ADMIN --- change only
  via the admin user view (registration can never self-assign roles).
\item
  2FA: progressive enforcement for privileged roles
  (\texttt{TWO\_FACTOR\_ENFORCE} flips from warn to require).
\item
  GDPR: data export (\texttt{POST\ /users/me/export/}), soft-delete +
  purge; minors\textquotesingle{} profiles non-public; parental consent
  dates.
\item
  Certificates: \texttt{manage.py\ issue\_certificates} (idempotent
  derivation; \texttt{-\/-notify} optional); revocation ledger for
  integrity cases.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{7. Incident recipes}\label{7-incident-recipes}
